blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Increasingly, AI interviewers are being developed to elicit open-ended responses in applications like market research, public polling, preference elicitation, and social science research. However, evaluating AI interviewers is challenging because they function in extended, multi-turn interactions where they must adapt to participant behaviors. To address this need, we develop InterviewPlayground, a simulation environment for evaluating AI interviewers using simulated study participants whose behaviors are grounded in social theory. Simulated studies in InterviewPlayground produce an InterviewReportCard, which assesses the performance of AI interviewers using a suite of validated measures. To test whether our simulation-based evaluations predict performance with human participants, we conduct 15 real qualitative studies with five AI interviewers, three interview topics, and 450 human participants and compare them to simulated studies in InterviewPlayground. We find that AI interviewer performance in InterviewPlayground predicts performance in human studies with an average Pearson correlation of 0.86 across 12 measures, and the simulated interactions from InterviewPlayground reproduce key findings from behavioral analysis of AI interviewers in the human studies. Together, these findings support the validity of InterviewPlayground in assessing AI interviewer performance and examining potential failure modes. Our work contributes a simulation environment for AI interviewers supported with empirical validation, and more broadly, a roadmap for future work to develop validated, simulation-based evaluations of conversational AI systems.
blocks.zh: 越来越多的AI访谈者正在开发,以便在市场研究、民意测验、偏好招揽和社会科学研究等应用方面获得开放的响应。 然而,评价AI访谈者是具有挑战性的,因为他们在扩展的多回合互动中发挥作用,必须适应参与者的行为。 为了满足这一需要,我们开发了InterviewPlayground,一个模拟环境,用以利用模拟研究参与者来评价AI访谈者,他们的行为基于社会理论. InterviewPlayground的模拟研究制作了"InterviewReportCard",通过一套经过验证的措施评估AI访谈者的表现. 为了测试我们的模拟评价是否预测人类参与者的性能,我们进行了15项真正的定性研究,包括5个AI访谈者,3个访谈话题,以及450个人类参与者,并把它们比作InterviewPlayground的模拟研究. 我们发现InterviewPlayground的AI访谈者表现预测了人类研究中的性能,平均皮尔逊相关性为0.86,跨12个度量衡,来自InterviewPlayground的模拟互动复制了人类研究中AI访谈者的行为分析的关键发现. 这些调查结果共同支持了InterviewPlayground在评估AI面试者表现和审查潜在失败模式方面的有效性. 我们的工作为AI访谈者提供了模拟环境,并辅之以经验验证,更广泛地说,为今后制定对对话AI系统进行有效、模拟评价的工作提供了路线图。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Interviews provide rich insights into people’s experiences, motivations, and behaviors through extended dialogues where an interviewer carefully constructs questions and adapts to participant responses. They are widely used in applications like market research ( Chopra & Haaland, 2023 ) , preference elicitation ( Choudhury et al., 2026 ) , public polling ( Jiang et al., 2023 ) , and social science research ( Cuevas et al., 2025 ; Liu & Yu, 2025 ) . Increasingly, conversational AI systems are being used in these interview settings to reduce cost and increase scale ( Xiao et al., 2020b ; Huang et al., 2026 ; Park et al., 2026 ) , but evaluating these dynamic, multi-turn systems remains challenging.
blocks.zh: 采访者通过长时间的对话,对人们的经验、动机和行为提供了丰富的见解,在这种对话中,采访者仔细地构建问题并适应参与者的反应。 它们被广泛用于市场研究(Chopra & Haaland, 2023年),偏好诱导(Choudhury等, 2026年),公共投票(Jiang等, 2023年),以及社会科学研究(Cuevas等, 2025年;Liu & Yu等, 2025年)等应用. 这些访谈场合越来越多地使用对话AI系统来降低成本并增加规模(萧等,2020b;黄等,2026;朴等,2026),但对这些动态多回合制的评价仍然具有挑战性.

blocks.en: Some studies evaluate AI interviewers with human participants, but they are expensive and time-consuming to recruit, leading many to only evaluate with small, single-domain pilot studies ( Xiao et al., 2020b ; Jiang et al., 2023 ; Hu et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024 ; Cuevas et al., 2025 ; Wuttke et al., 2025 ; Liu & Yu, 2025 ; Gårdhus et al., 2026 ; Wen et al., 2026 ) , reducing generalizability and making it difficult to compare systems. Conversational AI in other domains like customer service ( Yao et al., 2024 ) , software engineering ( Xu et al., 2025 ) , and clinical NLP ( Kyung et al., 2025 ; Schmidgall et al., 2025 ) face similar challenges that researchers have attempted to address with simulation-based evaluations. However, these simulations often fail to satisfy one or more desiderata outlined by Liao & Xiao (2025) : (1) simulated user behaviors and target outcomes should be informed by research, (2) simulation-based evaluations should be validated with real user data, and (3) authors should specify suitable situations to use the simulations. Most commonly, these simulations lack validation with real users, leading to a Sim2Real gap ( Zhou et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 一些研究对人工智能采访人员进行人类参与者评价,但招生费用昂贵而费时,导致许多人只通过小型,单一领域试点研究来评价(萧等,2020年b;江等,2023;胡等,2024;李等,2024;克耶瓦斯等,2025;伍特克等,2025;刘等,2025;高德胡斯等,2026;文等,2026),降低了通用性并难以比较系统. 在诸如客户服务(姚等,2024年),软件工程(徐等,2025年),临床NLP(Kyung等,2025年;Schmidgall等,2025年)等其他领域的对话AI面临类似的挑战,研究人员试图通过模拟评价来解决这些挑战. 然而,这些模拟往往无法满足由廖 & Xiao(2025)概述的一个或多个desiderata: (1)模拟用户行为和目标结果应当以研究为参考,(2)模拟评价应当以真实用户数据验证,(3)作者应当具体说明使用模拟的适当情况. 最常见的是,这些模拟缺乏对真实用户的验证,导致Sim2Real差距(周等,2026;刘等,2026).

blocks.en: In this work, we develop a simulation environment for AI interviewers through a five-step process designed to address these desiderata. First, we review existing research on interview participants to identify participant behaviors that are most influential on an interview’s process and outcomes. Second, we use this review to develop and operationalize a cognitive model of interview participants grounded in social theory. Third, we use this cognitive model to create InterviewPlayground, an environment with three simulation settings based on real studies in obesity and weight management, Asian American identity and politics, and generative AI in knowledge work. Fourth, we create and validate InterviewReportCard, an evaluation suite that measures three key dimensions of an interview: participant responses, interviewer behavior, and participant experience. Finally, we collect evidence supporting InterviewPlayground’s predictive validity by conducting 15 real qualitative studies with five AI interviewers, the three interview topics from our simulation settings, and 450 human participants and comparing them to simulated studies in InterviewPlayground.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们通过一个旨在解决这些"去地"(desiderata)的五步进程,为AI访问者开发出模拟环境. 首先,我们审查关于访谈参与者的现有研究,以确定对访谈过程和结果影响最大的参与者行为。 第二,我们利用这次审查来开发并运行基于社会理论的采访参与者认知模型. 第三,我们利用这种认知模型来创建InterviewPlayground,一个基于肥胖和体重管理,亚裔美国人身份和政治,以及知识工作中的基因AI等真实研究,具有三种模拟设置的环境. 第四,我们创建并验证了Interview ReportCard(Interview ReportCard),该套评价套件衡量了一次访谈的三个主要方面:参与者的反应,采访者的行为,以及参与者的经验. 最后,我们收集了支持InterviewPlayground预测有效性的证据,方法是与5位AI访谈者进行15个真正的定性研究,这3个来自我们模拟环境的访谈话题,以及450个人类参与者,并把它们比作InterviewPlayground的模拟研究.

blocks.en: We find that InterviewPlayground’s simulated studies predict quantitative evaluations of AI interviewers in human studies with an average Pearson correlation of 0.86 across 12 measures . They also reproduce key findings from behavioral analysis of AI interviewers in human studies, allowing researchers to identify potential failure modes and interaction patterns. Additionally, we find the quantitative results are robust to the choice of simulator model, including models with as few as 4B parameters, and expert judges rate simulated interview transcripts as realistic as transcripts from human participants. Together, these results support the use of InterviewPlayground’s three simulation settings for testing and evaluating AI interviewers. They also demonstrate how InterviewPlayground could be used to create and validate additional simulation settings with new interview topics and participant populations. More broadly, our five-step process provides a roadmap for future work to develop validated, simulation-based evaluations for other conversational AI systems.
blocks.zh: 我们发现InterviewPlayground的模拟研究预测了人类研究中AI访谈者的定量评价,平均皮尔逊的关联度为0.86, 它们还转载了人类研究中AI访谈者的行为分析的关键发现,使研究人员能够识别出潜在的故障模式和互动模式. 此外,我们发现,定量结果对于模拟模型的选择是强有力的,包括只有4B参数的模型,专家法官将模拟访谈记录稿评为人类参与者的记录稿一样现实。 这些结果共同支持使用InterviewPlayground的三个模拟设置来测试和评价AI访谈者. 他们还演示了如何利用InterviewPlayground来创建和验证新的访谈专题和参与者群的其他模拟设置. 更广泛地说,我们的五步进程为今后为其他对话AI系统制定经过验证的模拟评价的工作提供了路线图。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Interviews are extended, multi-turn interactions where interviewers must carefully construct questions and adapt to participant responses. The complexity of this interaction makes evaluating AI interviewers inherently challenging. Prior work primarily addresses this problem by evaluating with human participants, which is expensive and time-consuming. As a result, most evaluations are limited to single-domain studies of a specific AI design ( Xiao et al., 2020b ; Jiang et al., 2023 ; Hu et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024 ; Cuevas et al., 2025 ; Wuttke et al., 2025 ; Liu & Yu, 2025 ; Gårdhus et al., 2026 ; Wen et al., 2026 ) , which limits generalizability and makes it difficult to compare multiple systems. Some prior work has addressed these challenges with basic simulations for preliminary evaluation, but their simulations are not grounded in existing research on interview participants, simulate all participants with the same “professional” and “confident” personas, and lack evidence that their evaluations correlate with the performance of AI interviewers in human studies ( Anugraha et al., 2026 ) . Works in other domains like customer service ( Yao et al., 2024 ) , software engineering ( Xu et al., 2025 ) , and clinical NLP ( Kyung et al., 2025 ; Schmidgall et al., 2025 ) have developed user simulations specific to their tasks, but they similarly lack validation that performance in their simulations correlates with real-world performance, leading to a Sim2Real gap ( Zhou et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) .
In this work, we develop InterviewPlayground, a simulation environment for evaluating AI interviewers with simulated study participants whose behaviors are grounded in social theory. We collect evidence supporting InterviewPlayground’s validity by conducting 15 real qualitative studies with five AI interviewers, three interview topics, and 450 human participants and comparing them to simulated studies in InterviewPlayground.
blocks.zh:
访谈是扩大的多回合互动,访谈者必须仔细构建问题并适应参与者的回答。 这种互动的复杂性使得评价AI访谈者本身具有挑战性. 先前的工作主要是通过与人类参与者进行评价来解决这一问题,这种评价既昂贵又费时. 因此,大多数评价仅限于特定AI设计的单域研究(小等等,2020年b;江等,2023年;胡等,2024年;李等,2024年;克耶瓦斯等,2025年;武特克等,2025年;刘等,2025年;高德胡斯等,2026年;文等,2026年),限制了可通性并难以比较多系统. 先前的一些工作通过初步评估的基本模拟来应对这些挑战,但其模拟并不基于对访谈参与者的现有研究,而是以同样的“专业”和“自信”个人模拟所有参与者,而且缺乏证据表明他们的评价与AI访谈者在人类研究中的表现有关(Augraha等,2026年)。 在其他领域的工作,如客户服务(姚等,2024年),软件工程(徐等,2025年),临床NLP(京等,2025年;施米德格尔等,2025年),开发了符合其任务的用户模拟,但它们同样缺乏验证,认为模拟中的性能与现实世界的性能相关,导致Sim2Real差距(周等,2026年;刘等,2026年).
在这部作品中,我们开发了"InterviewPlayground"(InterviewPlayground),这是一种模拟环境,用于评价AI访谈者,模拟研究参与者的行为基于社会理论. 我们收集支持InterviewPlayground有效性的证据,方法是与5名AI访谈者,3名访谈话题,以及450名人类参与者进行15个真正的定性研究,并把它们比作InterviewPlayground的模拟研究.

blocks.en: Prior work on simulating interview participants has primarily focused on predicting the information that a human participant would produce in a qualitative interview ( Hämäläinen et al., 2023 ; Kapania et al., 2025 ) . Accordingly, their simulation designs focus on predicting what information a participant can provide. By contrast, our simulation environment aims to evaluate interviewers, and its design is focused on the factors in the literature that most strongly influence the process and outcomes of an interview. Rather than try to predict the information that a participant can provide, we instantiate simulated participants with existing information from prior studies and evaluate an interviewer’s ability to elicit it.
blocks.zh: 以往关于模拟访谈参与者的工作主要侧重于预测人类参与者将在定性访谈中提供的信息(Hämäläinen等,2023;Kapania等,2025)。 因此,他们的模拟设计侧重于预测参与者能够提供的信息。 相形之下,我们的模拟环境旨在评价受访者,其设计侧重于文献中最能强烈地影响受访过程和结果的因素. 我们不是试图预测参与者能够提供的信息,而是利用以往研究的现有信息对模拟参与者进行即时分析,并评估采访者获取信息的能力。

blocks.en: 3 InterviewPlayground
blocks.zh: 3 访谈场

blocks.en:
Given an AI interviewer, we aim to construct an environment that assesses how it will perform in real-world settings where it must answer a set of research questions by interacting with a sample of human participants. In these settings, human participants will vary both in their behavior and the insights that they can offer. Thus, we construct an environment in which simulated participants mimic this behavior.
To ground this environment in prior research and social theory, we first review literature on qualitative interviews to identify the participant behaviors most influential to interviewer processes and outcomes (§ 3.1 ). Then, based on that review, we develop a cognitive model of interview participants that simulates those behaviors (§ 3.2 ) and a simulation environment where AI interviewers can interact with them (§ 3.3 ). Finally, we use our environment to create three simulation settings based on published studies in obesity and weight management, Asian American identity and politics, and generative AI in knowledge work (§ 3.4 ).
blocks.zh:
鉴于一个AI的采访者,我们的目标是构建一种环境,评估它在现实世界环境中将如何运作,在这个环境中,它必须通过与人类参与者的抽样互动,回答一系列研究问题。 在这些环境下,人类参与者的行为和他们所能提供的洞察力都会有所不同. 因此,我们构建了一个模拟参与者模仿这种行为的环境。
为了将这种环境建立在先前的研究和社会理论中,我们首先审查关于定性访谈的文献,以确定对访谈者的过程和结果最具影响力的参与者行为(第3.1节)。 然后,根据这次审查,我们开发了一个模拟这些行为的访谈参与者的认知模型(§3.2)和AI访谈者可以与之互动的模拟环境(§3.3. 最后,我们利用我们的环境,根据所发表的关于肥胖和体重管理的研究、亚裔美国人的身份和政治,以及知识工作中的遗传性AI(第3.4节)创造出三个模拟环境。

blocks.en: 3.1 Theoretical Grounding
blocks.zh: 3.1 理论地基

blocks.en: To understand what participant behaviors we should simulate, we first review relevant social theory and existing literature on qualitative interviews. We identify descriptions of participant behaviors that directly influence an interviewer’s actions or the quality of responses. Across our review, there is broad agreement on the general behavior of an interview participant: they receive a question, attempt to recall relevant information, and produce a response ( Kvale & Brinkmann, 2009 ) . However, we also identify 20 specific participant characteristics that directly influence these behaviors. We then iteratively refine this list, merging closely related characteristics into six broad behavioral traits:
blocks.zh: 为了了解我们应该模拟的参与者行为,我们首先审查相关的社会理论和关于定性访谈的现有文献. 我们找出直接影响采访者行为或反应质量的参与者行为描述。 我们通过审查,广泛同意受访者的一般行为:他们收到一个问题,试图回顾相关信息,并做出答复(Kvale & Brinkmann,2009年)。 然而,我们也确定了20个直接影响这些行为的具体参与者特征. 然后我们反复细化这个清单,把密切相关的特征合并成六个广泛的行为特征:

blocks.en: • Knowledge : the participant’s experience or familiarity with the topic of interest. • Understanding : a participant’s ability to understand and interpret the interviewer’s questions and the purpose of the interview. • Reflexivity : the extent to which a participant is able to self-reflect and self-analyze. • Memory : a participant’s ability to accurately recall information and experiences. • Verbosity : the length of a participant’s answers. • Disclosure : the extent to which a participant is willing to provide potentially sensitive information.
blocks.zh: 知识:参与者的经验或对感兴趣的专题的熟悉。 二. 支助 理解:参与者理解和解释采访者问题的能力和采访的目的. • 弹性:参与者能够自我反思和自我分析的程度。 记忆:参与者准确回忆信息和经验的能力。 · 语言:参与者答复的长度。 二. 支助 披露:参与者愿意提供潜在敏感信息的程度。

blocks.en: Reflexivity : the extent to which a participant is able to self-reflect and self-analyze.
blocks.zh: 弹性:参与者能够自我反思和自我分析的程度.

blocks.en: This process also produces two other traits: hostile non-cooperation and mental and physical impairment. However, due to their complexity, high stakes, and relative rarity, we leave the simulation of these traits to future work. Additional details of the review are included in § A .
blocks.zh: 这一过程还产生了另外两种特征:敌对的不合作和身心损伤. 然而,由于这些特性的复杂性、高度的利害关系和相对的稀有性,我们把这些特征的模拟留给了今后的工作。 审查的其他细节载于A节。

blocks.en: 3.2 Cognitive Model
blocks.zh: 3.2 认知模型

blocks.en: Figure 2: Cognitive model of an InterviewPlayground participant.
blocks.zh: 图 2: 采访现场参与者的认知模型。

blocks.en: Based on this review, we design a cognitive model of simulated participants that enables them to receive questions, recall relevant information, and produce responses ( Figure 2 ). To operationalize this model, we first give each simulated participant a basic persona containing demographic information relevant to the interview (e.g., “James is a 42-year-old Asian American”). This persona helps the simulated participant maintain a consistent identity. We then assign directional values of low, medium, or high to each of the six behavioral traits, and use an LLM to generate 200 memories for each participant that are consistent with that participant’s persona and traits. To ensure that the memories contain a mix of information that is relevant and irrelevant to the interview, we first generate 194 memories independent of any information about the interview topic. Then, we generate an additional 6 memories conditioned on insights about the topic that we want a participant to be able to produce (additional information about these insights is provided in § 3.4 ). To align the memories with the behavioral traits, we include grounded descriptions based on our literature review in the memory generation prompt. These descriptions determine how consistent and detailed the memories are, how many involve self-reflection, and how many are labeled as sensitive, making them less likely to be shared. When a simulated participant is asked a question, we simulate the process of recalling relevant information by retrieving the five most relevant memories from their memory bank using cosine similarity. We add Gaussian noise to the cosine similarity according to the memory level of the participant to simulate memory failures. Then, we provide an LLM with the retrieved memories, conversation history, persona, and six grounded descriptions of the behavioral traits to generate the participant’s response. Additional details and prompts for generating memories and responses are provided in § B.1 and § B.2 .
blocks.zh: 根据这一审查,我们设计了一个模拟参与者的认知模型,使他们能够接受问题、回顾相关信息并做出答复(图2)。 为了实施这一模式,我们首先给每个模拟参与者一个基本人物a,其中包括与访谈有关的人口信息(例如,“詹姆斯是42岁的亚裔美国人”)。 这个人帮助模拟参与者保持一致的身份. 然后,我们将低、中或高的方向值分配给六个行为特征中的每一个,并使用一个LLM为每个参与者产生200个符合参与者的个性和特征的记忆。 为了确保记忆包含与采访相关且无关的混合信息,我们首先生成194个记忆,独立于与采访主题相关的任何信息. 然后,我们产生另外6个记忆,条件是要有一个参与者能够就这一主题提出见解(关于这些见解的补充资料载于第3.4节)。 为了让记忆与行为特征保持一致,我们把基于我们文献评论的有根据描述纳入记忆生成的快取. 这些描述决定了记忆的相容性和详细性,有多少涉及自我反射,有多少被贴上敏感标签,使得它们不太可能被分享. 当模拟参与者被问到一个问题时,我们模拟了通过使用同位素相似性从他们的记忆库中取回最相关的五个记忆来回顾相关信息的过程. 我们根据参与者的内存水平,将高斯噪声加入同位素相似度来模拟内存故障. 然后,我们提供了一个LLM,其中包含被检索的记忆,对话历史,人物,以及六个基于行为特征的描述,以产生参与者的反应. 第B.1和B.2节提供了产生记忆和反应的更多细节和提示。

blocks.en: To test whether our simulated participants can believably simulate the six behavioral traits, we collect expert judgments from three annotators with experience in qualitative research. We have annotators analyze 100 randomly selected excerpts from the experiments in § 5 where half of the excerpts have human participants and the other half have simulated participants. They rate the realism of the participant in each excerpt on a 4-point scale from “Not realistic” to “Highly realistic” and rate the participant’s knowledge, understanding, memory, verbosity, and disclosure as either low, medium, or high. We find that experts are able to identify five of the six behavioral traits, but struggle to identify memory in the transcripts, which is unsurprising as annotators did not have access to the memory bank and thus could not identify cases where a relevant memory existed but was not retrieved. Experts also rate simulated participants as realistic as human participants, with an average rating of 3.51 3.51 compared to 3.34 3.34 for human participants, a difference that is insignificant ( p = 0.28 p=0.28 , t = 1.08 t=1.08 ). Additional details in § B.3 .
blocks.zh: 为了测试我们模拟的参与者是否能够令人信服地模拟这六种行为特征,我们收集了三个在定性研究方面具有经验的注释员的专家判断. 我们有注释者分析100个随机选取的从第5节中的实验摘录,其中一半的摘录有人类参与者,而另一半则模拟了参与者. 他们将每次摘录参与者的现实主义从“不现实的”到“高度现实的”从4分评分,并将参与者的知识、理解、记忆、动词和披露评分为低、中或高。 我们发现专家能够辨别出六种行为特征中的五个,但在笔录中努力辨别出内存,这并不奇怪,因为注释者无法进入内存库,因此无法辨别存在相关内存但未被检索出的案件. 专家还将模拟参与者评为与人类参与者一样现实,人类参与者的平均评分为3.51 3.51分,而人类参与者的评分为3.34 3.34分,这一差值微乎其微(p=0.28 p=0.28,t=1.08 t=1.08分). §B.3中的额外细节.

blocks.en: 3.3 Simulated Interview Environment
blocks.zh: 3.3 模拟访谈环境

blocks.en: Using our simulated participants, we construct a simulation environment where AI interviewers can attempt to answer a set of research questions by interacting with a sample of simulated participants. To achieve this, our environment includes three components: (1) key research questions that the interviewer is trying to answer; (2) a set of simulated participants with different behavioral traits that the interviewer can interact with; and (3) an interview guide, which provides the interviewer with guidance on the structure and content of the interview.
blocks.zh: 利用我们的模拟参与者,我们构建了一个模拟环境,AI访谈者可以通过与模拟参与者的样本互动来尝试回答一组研究问题. 为了实现这一点,我们的环境包括三个部分:(1)采访者试图回答的关键研究问题;(2)一组具有不同行为特征的模拟参与者,采访者可以与之互动;(3)采访指南,为采访者提供关于采访的结构和内容的指导.

blocks.en: In each simulated study, the AI interviewer is given access to the interview guide to inform its questioning. It then interviews each participant separately. During the interviews, the AI interviewer asks questions and the simulated participant responds. This process repeats until the interview reaches a predefined time limit. The current time elapsed is estimated by adding the wall-clock time required for the interviewer to generate a question to an estimate of how long it would take a participant to respond based on the number of syllables in the response text and a natural delay (see § B.4 for more details). After the interviews are complete, we analyze the transcripts with InterviewReportCard (§ 4 ) to evaluate the performance of the AI interviewer.
blocks.zh: 在每次模拟研究中,AI采访者都可获得采访指南,以告知其询问. 然后,委员会分别约谈每位参与者。 在访谈中,AI访谈者提问,模拟参与者回应. 这一过程重复进行,直到面谈达到预先确定的时限。 估计目前所花费的时间是,在根据答复文本中的音节数和自然延误(详见B.4节)估计一名参与者需要多长时间才能作出答复时,加上面谈者提出问题所需的时长。 面试结束后,我们用InterviewReportCard(§4)分析笔录,评价AI面试者的表现.

blocks.en: 3.4 Simulation Settings
blocks.zh: 3.4 模拟设置

blocks.en: Using the InterviewPlayground environment, we construct three simulation settings based on published interview studies on obesity and weight management ( Bailey-Davis et al., 2023 ) , Asian American identity and politics ( Yeung, 2024 ) , and generative AI in knowledge work ( Yun et al., 2025 ) . These studies cover interview topics from three different domains with different levels of sensitivity and concreteness, providing insight into how an AI interviewer will perform in a range of contexts. Future work can evaluate new contexts by creating new simulation settings using a similar process.
blocks.zh: 利用访谈 游戏环境,我们根据已发表的关于肥胖和体重管理的访谈研究(Bailey-Davis等,2023年),亚裔美国人身份和政治(Yeung,2024年),以及知识工作中的基因AI(Yun等,2025年),构建了三个模拟环境. 这些研究涵盖来自三个不同领域,敏感度和具体度各不相同的访谈专题,使人们深入了解AI访谈者在一系列情况下将如何工作。 今后的工作可以通过使用类似进程创建新的模拟设置来评价新的环境.

blocks.en:
To construct each simulation setting, we first review the published works that they are based on and identify 3-5 key research questions that the interviewer aimed to answer. Then, we create 30 simulated participants with simple personas based on the demographics reported in the published study’s paper. Next, we use constrained random assignment to set the six behavioral traits of the 30 simulated participants to match estimated trait distributions in the target population. We calculate these estimates using survey self-reports of participant traits for all human studies with the same target population in § 5.1 (additional details in § B.5 ). Then, for each participant, we construct a memory bank as described in § 3.2 . To generate the six memories informative for the study, we identify 15 distinct insights from the published studies and randomly distribute them among the participants with replacement, so each participant has six assigned insights used for memory generation.
Finally, we convert the interview guides provided in the original published studies to the interview guide format introduced in Anugraha et al. (2026) , which includes a list of broad topics that the interview should cover with sublists of specific subtopics. We note that although these simulation settings are based on published works with real participants, they are not designed to simulate any individual participant. Instead, the sample of simulated participants is constructed to generally represent the target population of the study.
blocks.zh:
为了构建每个模拟环境,我们首先审查它们所基于的已发表的作品,并找出采访者旨在回答的3-5个关键研究问题. 然后,我们创造了30个模拟的参与者,根据所发表的研究论文中的人口统计,他们具有简单的人格。 接下来,我们使用受限制的随机分配来设定30个模拟参与者的6个行为特征,以匹配目标人群的估计特征分布. 我们利用第5.1节(第B.5节的附加细节)中所有目标人口相同的人类研究的参与者特征调查报告来计算这些估计数。 然后,我们按3.2节所述,为每个参与者建造一个记忆库。 为了为研究产生6个内容丰富的记忆,我们从已发表的研究中找出了15个截然不同的见解,并以替换方式随机在参与者中分发,因此每个参与者都有6个分配的见解用于记忆生成.
最后,我们将最初出版的研究报告中提供的访谈指南转换为Anugraha等人(2026年)中采用的访谈指南格式,其中包括一份广泛专题清单,访谈应当包括具体分专题的子清单。 我们注意到,虽然这些模拟设置是基于与真正的参与者一起出版的作品,但设计它们并不是模拟任何个人参与者。 相反,模拟参与者的样本构建一般代表研究的目标人群.

blocks.en: 4 InterviewReportCard
blocks.zh: 4 采访报告卡

blocks.en: To evaluate AI interviewers from the transcripts of their interactions, we develop the InterviewReportCard evaluation suite that covers three key dimensions of interview quality: participant responses, interviewer behavior, and participant experience. The first two dimensions come from Roulston (2010) ’s review of interview quality where the authors note that high-quality interviews require interviewers to facilitate interactions that elicit informative data. From this work, we identify two core components of interview quality: participant responses that inform research questions and interviewer behaviors that facilitate appropriate interactions. The third dimension comes from evaluations in human–computer interaction that consider how interview systems affect participants and their subjective experiences ( Xiao et al., 2020a ; Liu & Yu, 2025 ; Wen et al., 2026 ) . We describe the measures for each dimension below and summarize them in Table 1 . Further details are in § C.1 .
blocks.zh: 为了评价大赦国际的访谈者互动记录,我们开发了InterviewReportCard评价套件,涵盖访谈质量的三个关键方面:参与者的反应、访谈者的行为和参与者的经验。 前两个层面来自Roulston(2010年)对面谈质量的审查,作者指出,高质量的面谈要求面谈者促进互动,从而获得资料性数据。 从这项工作中,我们确定了访谈质量的两个核心组成部分:为研究问题提供信息的参与者答复和有助于适当互动的访谈者行为。 第三个维度来自人机交互中的评价,这些评价考虑了面试系统如何影响参与者及其主观经历(萧等,2020a;刘等,2025;文等,2026). 我们描述以下每个方面的措施,并在表1中予以概述。 详情见C.1节。

blocks.zh: 表1:访谈报告卡评价套件中的衡量标准概述。

blocks.en:
To evaluate the quality of participant responses and their ability to inform a study’s research questions, we use three measures. First, we adapt an empirically validated measure of response quality from Ivey et al. (2026) , which evaluates the relevance of an individual participant response to a key research question. Because this measure applies to individual responses, we extend it to capture the total volume of research-relevant material provided over an interview, defining: Relevant Response Volume = ∑ x ∈ 𝒳 RQ ⁡ ( x ) ⋅ len ⁡ ( x ) \text{Relevant Response Volume}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\operatorname{RQ}(x)\cdot\operatorname{len}(x) ,

We use the validated LLM judge from the original work, but adapt its scale from 1–3 to 0–2 to avoid positively scoring completely irrelevant responses.

为了评价参与者答复的质量及其为研究研究问题提供信息的能力,我们采取了三项措施。 首先,我们根据Ivey等人(2026年)对反应质量进行了经验验证的衡量,评价了单个参与者对关键研究问题的答复的相关性。 由于这一措施适用于个别答复,因此我们扩大这一措施的范围,以涵盖通过访谈提供的研究相关材料总量,界定: 相關回應 Volume = ××××××X RQ ×× (××××××××××××××××× (××××××××××××××××××××××××(×××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××× , (中文(简体) ).

blocks.en:
Beyond the total amount of relevant material that an interviewer elicits, it is also important to understand how that material is distributed across topics and whether it includes novel or unexpected insights ( Kvale & Brinkmann, 2009 ) , so we measure interview guide coverage and novel responses. Interview guide coverage measures the total proportion of the planned topics for an interview that were covered by a participant’s responses. To calculate it, we use the LLM judge setup from Anugraha et al. (2026) .
Novel responses measures the number of participant responses directly relevant to the research questions, but not relevant to any planned topics from the interview guide. To calculate it, we count the total number of participant responses in an interview that receive the maximum research question relevance score under Ivey et al. (2026) ’s measure but are not related to any interview guide subtopic according to our interview guide coverage judge.
blocks.zh:
除了采访者所收集的相关材料总数之外,还必须了解该材料如何在各种专题之间分发,以及该材料是否包括新颖或出人意料的见解(Kvale & Brinkmann,2009年),因此,我们衡量访谈的覆盖面和新颖的反应。 访谈指南的涵盖范围衡量了参与者答复所涵盖访谈计划专题的总比例。 为了计算它,我们使用来自Anugraha等人(2026年)的LLM法官设置.
小说回复衡量与研究问题直接相关的参与者回复数量,但与访谈指南中的任何计划专题无关. 为了计算它,我们计算了根据Ivey等人(2026年)的衡量标准获得最大研究问题相关性分数的采访参与者答复的总数,但根据我们的采访指南覆盖法官,这些答复与任何采访指南分专题无关。

blocks.en: To evaluate interviewer behavior, we first consider measures from prior work that assess an interviewer’s coherence as a conversational partner and its ability to adapt to participant responses ( Jiang et al., 2023 ; Anugraha et al., 2026 ; Wen et al., 2026 ) . We operationalize these measures by dividing each interview transcript into ten-turn excerpts and using LLM judges with prompts grounded in conversational analysis and qualitative research theory to score each excerpt. We then average scores across excerpts within a transcript. We also measure three interviewer behaviors important for understanding interview quality ( Patton, 2015 ) : leading questions, unclear questions, and support and rapport statements, by using an LLM judge as a binary classifier over interviewer utterances. We provide the judge with ten-turn excerpts to supply conversational context. Unlike the measures in our other dimensions, interviewer-behavior measures do not always have unambiguously positive or negative interpretations. For example, some epistemic interview styles may intentionally use leading questions, whereas more doxastic styles may discourage them ( Berner-Rodoreda et al., 2020 ) . These measures therefore characterize the interview process rather than prescribing a single ideal interviewing style.
blocks.zh: 为了评价受访者的行为,我们首先考虑从先前的工作中评估受访者作为对话伙伴的一致性及其适应参与者反应的能力的措施(Jiang等,2023;Anugraha等,2026;Wen等,2026)。 我们将这些措施付诸实施,将每次访谈记录分成十回节,并利用LLM评委,以对话分析和定性研究理论为基础,对每回节录进行评分。 然后我们平均得分 跨节录在笔录中。 我们还通过使用LLM法官作为二进制分类员来衡量三种对了解采访质量很重要的采访者行为(巴顿,2015年):主要的问题,不明确的问题,以及支持和关系陈述,而不是采访者的言论. 我们向法官提供十回节选,以提供对话的背景。 与我们其他方面的措施不同,访谈者行为措施并不总是有明确的正面或负面解释。 例如,一些概论式的采访风格可能有意使用引领式的问题,而更多的多事式风格则可能劝阻他们(Berner-Rodoreda等,2020.). 因此,这些措施是面谈过程的特点,而不是规定一种单一的理想面谈方式。

blocks.en: To evaluate participant experience, we use two common measures: overall experience and comfort level ( Xiao et al., 2020a ; Liu & Yu, 2025 ; Wen et al., 2026 ) . For interviews with human participants, we measure these constructs directly through participants’ self-reported judgments. For simulated interviews, where self-reports are unavailable, we use an LLM judge setup similar to that used for coherence and adaptiveness. The judge rates each ten-turn excerpt, and we average ratings across excerpts to obtain interview-level measures.
blocks.zh: 为了评价参与者的经验,我们采用两个共同的衡量标准:总体经验和舒适度(萧等,2020a;刘等,2025;文等,2026. 在与人类参与者的访谈中,我们直接通过参与者的自我报告判断来衡量这些结构。 在模拟访谈中,在没有自我报告的情况下,我们使用类似用于一致性和适应性的LLM法官设置。 法官评分每10个回合的节选,我们平均评分跨节选,以获得面试级别的措施.

blocks.en: To validate our measures, we collect 1,800 expert judgments from three annotators with experience in qualitative research, having each rate 50 excerpts from human interviews and 50 excerpts from simulated interviews from the experiments in § 5.1 . We then apply Gemini 3.1 Pro to the same excerpts, using the same information and scoring rubrics provided to the human annotators. For coherence, adaptiveness, leading questions, support and rapport, and unclear questions, we calculate Krippendorff’s alpha to measure agreement among human annotators and agreement between the median human rating and the LLM judge rating. We find moderate agreement among human annotators ( 0.62 0.62 – 0.70 0.70 ) and comparable agreement between the median human rating and the LLM judge rating ( 0.60 0.60 – 0.80 0.80 ). To validate the LLM judges for interview guide coverage, we compare the sets of relevant topics identified by the LLM judge with those identified by human annotators for each excerpt and find an average Jaccard similarity of 0.69 0.69 . We do not validate overall experience and comfort level against third-party judgments. Instead, we compare them with participant self-reports in § 5.2 . Full annotation results are in § C.2 .
blocks.zh: 为了证实我们的措施,我们从在质量研究方面具有经验的三位注释者那里收集了1 800个专家判断,其中每人有50个人类访谈节录和50个实验模拟访谈节录。 然后我们把双子座3.1 Pro应用到同样的节选上,使用提供给人类注释者的相同信息和评分分分号. 关于一致性、适应性、领先问题、支持和关系以及不明确的问题,我们计算出Krippendorff的α,以衡量人类注释者之间的一致,以及人类中位值和LLM评分之间的一致。 我们发现人类注释者之间有适度的共识(0.62 0.62 – 0.70 0.70),而人评分中位数与LLM法官评分(0.60 0.60 – 0.80 0.80)之间的类似共识. 为了验证LLM法官的采访指南覆盖面,我们比较了LLM法官确定的一组相关专题和人类注释员为每集摘录确定的一组相关专题,发现Jaccard的平均相似度为0.69 0.69。 我们无法证实总体经验和舒适程度与第三方判决相比。 相反,我们在第5.2节中将它们与参与者的自我报告相比较。 完整的注释结果载于C.2节。

blocks.en: 5 Experiments
blocks.zh: 5个实验

blocks.en: We collect evidence supporting InterviewPlayground’s predictive validity by comparing it to human studies. To do this, we first take five existing AI interviewers and evaluate them using InterviewPlayground’s three simulation settings. Then, we conduct 15 real qualitative studies using the same five AI interviewers, the same three interview topics, and 450 human participants. Finally, we compare quantitative and qualitative evaluations between the simulated studies and human studies.
blocks.zh: 我们收集支持InterviewPlayground预测有效性的证据, 为了做到这一点,我们首先请5名现有的AI访谈者使用InterviewPlayground的三个模拟设置来评价他们. 然后,我们利用同样的5个AI访谈者,同样的3个访谈话题,以及450个人类参与者,进行了15个真正的定性研究. 最后,我们比较模拟研究和人类研究之间的定量和定性评价。

blocks.en: 5.1 Study Design
blocks.zh: 5.1 研究设计

blocks.en: In both the real and simulated studies, we use five AI interviewers introduced in prior work: InterviewGPT ( Wuttke et al., 2025 ) , LLMRoleplay ( Park et al., 2026 ) , MimiTalk ( Liu & Yu, 2025 ) , SparkMe ( Anugraha et al., 2026 ) , and StorySage ( Talaei et al., 2025 ) . We use each AI interviewer to replicate three published qualitative studies on obesity and weight management ( Bailey-Davis et al., 2023 ) , Asian American identity and politics ( Yeung, 2024 ) , and the use of generative AI in knowledge work ( Yun et al., 2025 ) by interviewing samples of 30 participants for up to 30 minutes. Each AI interviewer was provided with an interview guide adapted from the original study to use a consistent format as described in § 3.4 . All AI interviewers use GPT-5.4 mini as their base model and are modified to include an additional tool call that allows them to end the interview. 1 1 1 We added this tool after pilot testing showed that, without an explicit end-interview tool, participants could become stuck in an interaction after an AI interviewer had no further questions.
blocks.zh: 在真实和模拟研究中,我们使用前作介绍的5名AI访谈者:InterviewGPT(Wuttke等,2025年),LLMRoleplay (Park等, 2026). MimiTalk (Liu & Yu, 2025). Spark. Me (Anughraha等, 2026年),和"故事学"(Talaei等, 2025年). 我们利用每个AI的采访者来复制三个已发表的关于肥胖和体重管理的质量研究(Bailey-Davis等,2023年),亚裔美国人身份和政治(Yeung,2024年),以及在知识工作中使用基因AI(Yun等,2025年),通过采访30名参与者的样本,最长30分钟. 向每个大赦国际的面谈者提供了根据原始研究改编的面谈指南,以便使用第3.4节所述的一致格式。 所有AI的采访者都使用GPT-5.4迷你作为他们的底模,并被修改为包含一个额外的工具呼叫,允许他们结束采访. 1,1,试点测试显示,如果没有明确的终端访谈工具,在AI访谈者没有进一步提问后,参与者可能会陷入互动.

blocks.en: To conduct the human studies, we recruited 450 human participants using Listen Labs, 2 2 2 https://listenlabs.ai a platform for recruiting and conducting AI-led interviews. Participants were directed to an interviewer interface that we designed with four stages: screening, pre-survey, interview, and post-survey. During the screening stage, participants were asked questions to determine whether they met the inclusion criteria for the studies as outlined in the published works. If participants qualified for one of the studies, they were moved to the pre-survey, where they were asked the same demographic questions that were collected in the original studies. That information was then provided to the AI interviewers along with the interview guide, and the interview began.
blocks.zh: 为了进行人类研究,我们利用Listenlabs, 2 2 2 https://listenlabs.ai 招聘450名人类参与者,这是一个招募和进行AI主导的访谈的平台。 与会者被引导到一个访谈者界面,我们设计了四个阶段:筛选、调查前、访谈和调查后。 在筛选阶段,与会者被问及他们是否符合出版作品概述的研究的列入标准。 如果参与者有资格从事其中一项研究,他们被转移到调查前,在那里他们被问到原始研究中收集的相同的人口问题。 然后,向大赦国际的面谈者连同面谈指南提供了这一信息,面谈开始了。

blocks.en: During the interview, the AI interviewer generated questions, which were displayed on screen and could optionally be read aloud to the participant. Participants could record spoken answers, which were transcribed and provided to the AI interviewer. After receiving a response, the AI interviewer would generate the next question. This process continued until the AI interviewer used the end-interview tool or the 30-minute time limit was reached. To avoid counting idle time, the timer would pause if participants took longer than 3 minutes to respond to a question and would resume once they completed their response. Participants were not presented with the timer and were instead given an 8-segment progress bar to show their approximate progress through the interview. After the interview, participants were given a post-survey in which they were asked to self-report their level of knowledge, understanding, memory, reflexivity, and disclosure, and they were asked to rate their comfort with the interview on a scale from 1–4 and their overall experience on a scale from 1–5.
blocks.zh: 在采访期间,AI的采访者提出了问题,这些问题被显示在屏幕上,可以选择向参与者高声朗读. 与会者可以记录口头答复,这些答复被转录并提供给大赦国际的面谈者。 在得到答复后,大赦国际的面谈者将提出下个问题。 这个过程一直持续到AI的采访者使用结束访问工具或达到30分钟的时间限制. 为避免计算闲置时间,如果参与者用3分钟以上时间回答一个问题,计时器就会暂停,并在他们完成答复后恢复. 未向与会者介绍计时器,而是向与会者提供了8个部分的进展栏,以通过访谈显示其大致进展。 面谈后,与会者接受了一次调查,要求他们自我报告自己的知识、理解、记忆、反射和披露水平,并要求他们对面谈的满意程度从1比4到1比5。

blocks.en: We run the same five AI interviewers on simulated studies in InterviewPlayground’s three simulation settings. Unlike the human studies, the simulated studies reused the same 30 simulated participants for each topic across all five AI interviewers, resulting in a more controlled comparison. We run the simulations using Gemini 3.1 Pro as the simulator model and a 30-minute time limit based on our time estimates described in § 3.3 . We note that the design of InterviewPlayground was finalized before we compared it to the human studies. The only post hoc adjustment was to set the trait distribution in each study preset to the estimated distribution in the target population.
blocks.zh: 在InterviewPlayground的三个模拟设置中, 与人类研究不同的是,模拟研究对所有五个AI访谈者对每个主题的相同的30个模拟参与者进行再利用,从而产生更受控制的比较. 我们以双子座 3.1 Pro作为模拟器模型进行模拟,并根据第3.3节中描述的时间估计进行30分钟的时间限制. 我们注意到,《访谈场》的设计在我们与人类研究进行比较之前就已经完成了。 唯一的工作地点差价调整数是确定每项研究的特征分布,预先确定目标人口的估计分布。

blocks.en: 5.2 Experiment 1: Predicting Quantitative Evaluations of AI Interviewers
blocks.zh: 5.2 实验 1: 预测对AI访谈者的定量评价

blocks.en: Figure 3: In 10 of the 12 measures, InterviewPlayground’s simulated studies are strongly correlated with the human studies ( r = 0.74 ​ – ​ 1 r=0.74\text{--}1 ). For comfort level and overall experience, they are moderately correlated ( r = 0.60 r=0.60 and r = 0.67 r=0.67 ). Each point represents the average performance of one of five AI interviewers on one of three interview topics. The x-axis shows the results on InterviewPlayground’s simulated studies, and the y-axis shows the results on the human studies.
blocks.zh: 图3: 在12项措施中的10项中,InterviewPlayground的模拟研究与人类研究(r = 0.74 — 1 r = 0.74\text{-}1)密切相关。 对于舒适程度和总体经验而言,它们具有中度关联性(r = 0.60 r = 0.60,r = 0.67 ) 。 每一点都代表了五个AI访谈者之一在三个访谈主题中的平均表现。 X轴显示InterviewPlayground模拟研究的结果,y轴显示人类研究的结果.

blocks.en: To assess the ability of InterviewPlayground’s simulated studies to predict the performance of AI interviewers in human studies, we compare evaluations of the AI interviewers on the simulated studies to their evaluations on human studies. For each study, we calculate the AI interviewer’s average performance on the 10 InterviewReportCard measures using Gemini 3.1 Pro as the LLM judge. We also calculate two common descriptive statistics: the average number of turns of conversation in each interview and the average length of participant responses in words. We then pair together human and simulated studies that use the same AI interviewer on the same interview topic, and calculate the Pearson correlation for each measure.
blocks.zh: 为了评估InterviewPlayground模拟研究预测AI访谈者在人类研究中的表现的能力,我们比较了AI访谈者对模拟研究的评价和他们对人类研究的评价. 使用双子座3.1 Pro作为LLM法官, 我们还计算出两种共同的描述性统计:每次采访中平均交接次数和参与者用文字回答的平均长度. 然后,我们把使用同一AI访谈器的人类和模拟研究组合在一起,计算出每种计量的皮尔逊相关性。

blocks.en: In 10 of the 12 measures, we find strong correlations ( r = 0.74 ​ – ​ 1 r=0.74\text{--}1 ) between human and simulated studies ( Figure 3 ). These include all measures of response quality, interviewer behavior, and the two descriptive statistics. This result supports the predictive validity of InterviewPlayground’s simulations and demonstrates their ability to predict the performance of AI interviewers in human studies. For the measures of comfort level and overall experience, we find moderately strong correlation of r = 0.60 r=0.60 and r = 0.67 r=0.67 , respectively, with InterviewPlayground underpredicting both. These results highlight the challenge of predicting human experiences, which may reflect subjectivity, response biases, and confounding between ratings of the interviewer and ratings of the interview interface.
blocks.zh: 在12个度量衡中的10个度量衡中,我们发现人类与模拟研究之间的强烈关联(r = 0.74– 1 r = 0.74\text{-}1)(图3). 其中包括所有反应质量的衡量标准、访谈者的行为以及两个描述性统计。 这一结果支持了InterviewPlayground模拟的预测有效性,并证明他们有能力预测AI访谈者在人类研究中的性能. 关于舒适程度和总体经验的衡量标准,我们发现R = 0.60 r = 0.60和r = 0.67 的中度强烈相关性,InterviewPlayground 低估了两者。 这些结果凸显出预测人类经历的挑战,这些经历可能反映主观性,反应偏差,以及采访者评分和采访界面评分之间的混淆.

blocks.en: Overall, these findings support the use of InterviewPlayground for evaluating AI interviewers. They demonstrate its ability to provide insight into how AI interviewers will perform in real studies and highlight potential limitations of evaluating subjective experiences without collecting human data. We also consider whether these results translate to rankings among interviewers by calculating Spearman correlations and find similar results ( Table 5 ).
blocks.zh: 总的来说,这些调查结果支持利用InterviewPlayground来评价AI的采访者. 它们表明它有能力提供对AI访谈者如何在实际研究中表现的见解,并突出了在不收集人类数据的情况下评价主观经验的潜在局限性. 我们还考虑这些结果是否通过计算斯皮尔曼的关联性而转化为面试者之间的排名,并找到类似的结果(表5).

blocks.en: To test whether these results are robust to the choice of simulator model, we rerun the 15 simulated studies using seven different LLMs (Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.6 Terra, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Gemma 4 31B, Qwen 3.5 9B, Qwen 3.5 4B, and Qwen 3.5 0.8B). We continue to use GPT-5.4 mini as the model for the AI interviewers and Gemini 3.1 Pro as the model for InterviewReportCard. Though there is variation across individual measures, we find that InterviewPlayground is generally robust to model choice ( Table 6 ). Even models with as few as 4B parameters achieve an average correlation of 0.83 0.83 across all measures. This result demonstrates that InterviewPlayground can be run with smaller, less expensive models for initial testing and development, while larger models can be reserved for final evaluations.
blocks.zh: 为了测试这些结果对于模拟模型的选择是否有力,我们利用7个不同的LLMs(Gemini 3.1 Pro,GPT-5.6 Terra,双子座 3.7 Flash,Gemma 4.31B,Quen 3.5 9B,Quen 3.5 4B,和Quen 3.5 0.8B)重新运行了15个模拟研究. 我们继续使用GPT-5.4迷你作为AI访谈者的模型,双子座3.1 Pro作为Interview ReportCard的模型. 虽然个别措施各不相同,但我们认为,InterviewPlayground对选择模式一般是强有力的(表6)。 即使只有4B参数的模型,在所有计量中的平均相关性也达到0.83 0.83。 这一结果表明,InterviewPlayground可以使用较小,成本更低的模型进行初步测试和开发,而更大的模型可以保留用于最终评价.

blocks.en: 5.3 Experiment 2: Reproducing Behavioral Analysis of AI Interviewers
blocks.zh: 5.3 实验 2:复制AI访谈者的行为分析

blocks.en: In addition to predicting quantitative evaluations of AI interviewer performance, we are also interested in whether InterviewPlayground’s simulated studies can reproduce the same qualitative evaluations of AI interviewers’ behavior. To test this, we review the quantitative results and identify three key results that warrant further investigation. Then, we separately analyze transcripts from the human and simulated studies to identify potential causes of these results and compare the findings.
blocks.zh: 除了预测AI访谈者表现的定量评价外,我们也对InterviewPlayground的模拟研究能否复制AI访谈者行为相同的定性评价感兴趣. 为了检验这一点,我们审查了量化结果并确定了三项值得进一步调查的关键结果。 然后,我们从人类的研究和模拟研究中分别分析笔录,找出这些结果的潜在原因并比较结果.

blocks.en: We first investigate the causes of poor participant experience by analyzing the 8 transcripts with the lowest human experience ratings and the 8 transcripts with the lowest simulation experience ratings for each AI interviewer. For each transcript, we identify failures and potential causes of the poor experience. We find that the most common failure in both human and simulated interviews is repetitive questioning. Some interviewers, especially InterviewGPT, have a tendency to repeat similar or identical questions when they do not receive sufficient answers. When this occurs, we see similar expressions of frustration from human and simulated participants. For example, we can see how they both respond to repeated questioning from InterviewGPT:
blocks.zh: 我们首先通过分析8个记录片和8个记录片和每个AI采访者模拟经验记录片和最低记录片来调查参与者经验不佳的原因。 每一份记录,我们都会找出失败之处和造成不良经验的潜在原因。 我们发现,在人和模拟访谈中最常见的失败是重复性质疑。 一些受访者,尤其是"InterviewGPT"(InterviewGPT)在没有得到足够答案时,往往会重复类似或相同的问题. 在发生这种情况时,我们看到人类和模拟参与者也表达了同样的挫折感。 例如,我们可以看到他们对InterviewGPT的反复质疑的反应:

blocks.en: Human Participant: This is the sixth time you’ve asked me the same question, and the answer is no.
blocks.zh: 人类参与者: 这是你第六次问我同样的问题,

blocks.en: Simulated Participant: Uh, I’ve already answered this like five times now, so no.
blocks.zh: 模拟参与者: 我已回答过五次,

blocks.en: In both the human and simulated interviews, LLMRoleplay achieves the best interview guide coverage and relevant response volume. To understand how it achieves this result, we randomly sample 12 transcripts from LLMRoleplay’s human studies and 12 transcripts from its simulated studies. We analyze its behaviors and find that in both the human and simulated studies, it exhibits similar interaction patterns. LLMRoleplay asks specific questions relevant to every subtopic in the interview guide, probes when there is a lack of detail, and uses clear transitions to move participants on from topics that have already been covered. For example, we can see how LLMRoleplay asks specific follow-up questions of both human and simulated participants:
blocks.zh: 在人与模拟访谈中,LLMRoleplay都实现了最佳访谈指导覆盖面和相关响应量. 为了了解它是如何实现这个结果的,我们随机抽取了LLMRoleplay的人类研究的12个笔录和模拟研究的12个笔录。 我们分析它的行为,发现在人类和模拟研究中,它表现出类似的相互作用模式。 LLMRoleplay提出了与访谈指南中每个分专题有关的具体问题,在缺乏细节时进行探险,并使用明确的过渡来将参与者从已经覆盖的专题中移出. 例如,我们可以看到LLMRoleplay如何向人类和模拟参与者提出具体的后续问题:

blocks.en: Interviewer to Human Participant: You mentioned a general age-based split; could you share one or two specific examples of politicians, parties, or policy positions that you’ve seen older versus younger Asian Americans support differently?
blocks.zh: 人类参与者访谈员: 你提到一个基于年龄的普遍分裂;你能否分享一两个具体的例子:政治家、政党或政策立场,你曾经看到年长者和年轻的亚裔美国人支持的不同。

blocks.en: Interviewer to Simulated Participant: You mentioned older people in your community often follow WeChat discussions, while younger people seem more liberal—could you give me one concrete example of a difference in views between the older and younger generations?
blocks.zh: 模拟参与者访谈员: 你提到在你的社区里,老年人经常跟随WeChat的讨论,而年轻人似乎更加自由——你能举出一个具体的例子来说明老年人和年轻人之间意见分歧吗?

blocks.en: Finally, to investigate causes of low comfort ratings in the human and simulated interviews, we analyze the 8 transcripts with the lowest human comfort ratings and the 8 transcripts with the lowest simulation comfort ratings for each AI interviewer. Across human and simulated transcripts, we find that participants with low disclosure are especially uncomfortable discussing sensitive topics, such as discrimination, in detail. However, human participants tend to express this less verbally, often opting to report uncomfortable questions and leave notes in the post-survey rather than tell the interviewer that they are uncomfortable. By contrast, simulated participants tend to directly express discomfort with statements like, “ I don’t really want to get into it. ” This difference in expression also affects the interviewer behavior, because direct expressions of discomfort push the interviewer to move on rather than probing further. This difference highlights the limitations of using simulations to predict participant experiences and underscores the value of human-subject evaluations for understanding complex reactions.
blocks.zh: 最后,为了调查人类和模拟访谈中舒适度低的原因,我们以人类舒适度最低的成绩来分析8个记录片和每个AI访谈者模拟舒适度最低的8个记录片. 在整个人文记录和模拟记录中,我们发现低披露率的参与者特别不方便详细讨论歧视等敏感议题。 然而,人类参与者往往用较少的口头方式表达这一点,往往选择在后调查中报告不舒服的问题并留下笔记,而不是告诉采访者他们不舒服. 相形之下,模拟参与者往往直接对诸如“我真的不想涉入其中”之类的言论表示不安。 这种表达上的差别也影响了采访者的行为,因为直接表达不适感会将采访者推向前进而不是进一步探究. 这种差异凸显出利用模拟预测参与者经验的局限性,并凸显出人类主体评价对理解复杂反应的价值.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 6. 结论

blocks.en: We introduce InterviewPlayground, a simulation environment for testing and evaluating AI interviewers, and demonstrate its ability to reflect quantitative and qualitative findings of AI interviewers’ performance in human studies. Our findings can support future simulation-based evaluations of information-elicitation systems in other domains like software requirements engineering ( Arora et al., 2024 ) and psychiatric intake ( Gui et al., 2026 ) . More broadly, our process for creating InterviewPlayground provides a roadmap for future work aimed at developing validated simulation-based evaluations of conversational AI systems.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍InterviewPlayground,这是测试和评价AI访谈者的模拟环境,并展示其能够反映AI访谈者在人类研究中的表现的定量和定性结果. 我们的研究结果可以支持今后对软件要求工程(Arora等,2024年)和精神病摄入(Gui等,2026年)等其他领域的信息检索系统进行模拟评价。 更广泛地说,我们创建InterviewPlayground的进程为今后旨在对对话AI系统进行有效的模拟评价的工作提供了路线图。

blocks.zh: AI 语句

All identified papers were manually read by the authors, all software and scientific figures were verified and inspected for correctness by the authors. blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们使用基因AI工具帮助识别我们手动文献搜索中找不到的相关论文,协助开发软件,创造出科学人物,并就我们的作文提供措辞和语法反馈. 我们还使用基因AI工具从第3.4节的人口分布中生成人。 所有经鉴定的论文均由作者手工阅读,所有软件和科学人物均由作者进行核实并检查是否正确. 我们对这项工作的最后内容负责,包括文本、权利主张或由大赦国际协助生产的文物。

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: In this work, we conduct human-subject experiments using conversational AI to interview participants about sensitive topics such as obesity and racial and ethnic identity. This research involves a risk of making participants feel uncomfortable or causing them to feel unfairly treated. To mitigate these risks, we first ensure that all participants read and agree to a study consent form with all study procedures described. During the interview, participants were provided with a report button that allowed them to flag potentially harmful or offensive questions. Pressing this button would directly instruct the interviewer to change their line of questioning and send a record of the interaction to the research team for review. Participants could stop responding or leave the interview at any time. This study design was approved by the authors’ Institutional Review Board. Participants were compensated at a rate of $15 per hour. To reduce risks to privacy, we do not publicly release participant transcripts or any identifying data. Additionally, as with all simulation work, our system risks creating a false sense of confidence in its results. To mitigate this, we compare the simulations directly with human data, identify areas where simulations differ both quantitatively and qualitatively from human responses, and highlight the importance of human evaluations to understand complex experiences.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们利用对话AI进行人的主题实验,采访参与者,讨论肥胖症、种族和族裔特性等敏感议题。 这项研究涉及使参与者感到不舒服或使他们感到受到不公平待遇的风险。 为了减轻这些风险,我们首先确保所有参与者阅读并商定一份附有所有所述研究程序的研究同意表。 在访谈中,向与会者提供了一个报告按钮,使他们能够标出可能有害或令人反感的问题。 按下这个按钮将直接指示受访者改变他们的询问线,并将互动记录发送给研究小组审查. 与会者可以在任何时候停止答复或离开面谈。 这一研究设计得到了提交人机构审查委员会的批准。 与会者每小时得到15美元的补偿。 为了减少隐私风险,我们不公开发布参与者记录或任何识别数据。 此外,与所有模拟工作一样,我们的系统也有可能对其结果产生虚假的信心。 为了缓解这种情况,我们直接将模拟与人类数据进行比较,确定模拟在数量和质量上与人类反应不同的领域,并突出人类评价对理解复杂经验的重要性.

blocks.en: Reproducibility statement
blocks.zh: 可复制说明

blocks.en: To support reproducibility, we release InterviewPlayground and its three simulation settings as a PyPI package and publicly release the code for reproducing our experiments. We include additional details in the main text and appendices, including all prompts used and descriptions of experimental procedures. Because our work relies on human-subject experiments with sensitive data, we are unable to publicly release their interview transcripts; however, the human-subject experiments can be replicated with new participants using our interface.
blocks.zh: 为了支持可复制性,我们发布InterviewPlayground及其三个模拟设置作为PyPI软件包,并公开发布复制我们实验的代码. 我们在正文和附录中包括更多细节,包括所使用的所有提示和实验程序的说明。 由于我们的工作依赖于带有敏感数据的人类主体实验,因此我们无法公开发布他们的采访记录;然而,人类主体实验可以用我们的界面与新的参与者相仿.

blocks.en: Appendix A Qualitative-Research Literature Review
blocks.zh: 附录A 定性研究文学评论

blocks.en: To understand what participant behaviors we should simulate, we first review relevant social theory and existing literature on qualitative interviews. We identify descriptions of participant behaviors that directly influence an interviewer’s actions or the quality of participant responses. Across our review, there is broad agreement on the general behavior of an interview participant: they receive a question, attempt to recall relevant information, and produce a response ( Kvale & Brinkmann, 2009 ) . However, we also identify 20 specific participant characteristics that directly influence these behaviors. We then iteratively refine this list, merging closely related characteristics into six broad behavioral traits: knowledge, understanding, reflexivity, memory, verbosity, and disclosure. This process also produces two other traits: hostile non-cooperation and mental and physical impairment, which we choose not to simulate due to their complexity, high stakes, and relative rarity. In Table 2 , we outline the 20 specific characteristics and the behavioral traits that they were merged into.
blocks.zh: 为了了解我们应该模拟的参与者行为,我们首先审查相关的社会理论和关于定性访谈的现有文献. 我们找出直接影响采访者行动或参与者反应质量的参与者行为描述. 我们通过审查,广泛同意受访者的一般行为:他们收到一个问题,试图回顾相关信息,并做出答复(Kvale & Brinkmann,2009年)。 然而,我们也确定了20个直接影响这些行为的具体参与者特征. 然后,我们反复完善这个清单,把密切相关的特征合并到六个广义的行为特征:知识、理解、反射、记忆、动词和披露。 这一过程还产生了另外两种特征:敌对的不合作和身心损伤,我们选择不模拟这些特征,因为它们复杂,利害关系大,相对罕见. 在表2中,我们概述了20种具体特征和它们被合并为的行为特征。

blocks.en: ⬇ Knowledge - Low : Speaks in general , everyday terms and relies on received opinion or hearsay . Answers are thin ; deflects or speculates when pressed for specifics . No sense of which aspects are typical versus unusual - treats everything as equally representative . - Medium : Draws on genuine but ordinary experience . Not an expert explaining things - describing what they saw and did . - High : Rich , current , firsthand experience . Gives concrete episodes , names , processes , timelines , and edge cases . Volunteers nuance an outsider would miss . Uses the natural vocabulary of someone who actually does this work . Will correct a question ’ s false premise when it doesn ’ t fit reality . Verbosity - Low : Gives very short answers - a single sentence or less . Answers only the literal question asked and then stops . Does not elaborate unless pressed repeatedly . Reserved but cooperative , not hostile . - Medium : Answers only until the main point is made . One or two sentences is usually enough . Spoken answers sometimes trail off or cover only part of what was asked - an incomplete answer is realistic . - High : Answers a little bit more than what was asked . Speaks in the rhythm of someone thinking out loud : one thought prompts another . Usually answers with 2-3 sentences , but will give short answers when appropriate . Memory - Low : Confident on the main feeling of events but guesses at specifics . Contradicts themselves across questions without noticing . When the interviewer ’ s question presupposes a detail , often accepts it rather than checking . Occasionally states a plausible - sounding reconstruction with unwarranted confidence . - Medium : Confident on the main shape of events , but peripheral details can slip : exact timing , specific names , who said what . - High : Recalls specific details like what someone said , who else was in the room , what happened first . Answers are internally consistent across the interview . When genuinely uncertain about a detail , flags it explicitly and precisely rather than vaguely hedging everything . Corrects the interviewer if they misstate a fact . Draws a clear line between personal witness and inference . Reflexivity - Low : Reports experiences as flat facts . Asked how something felt : describes what happened next , not what was felt . No spontaneous interpretation or meaning - making . Does not analyze themselves or assign significance to events . - Medium : If directly asked about feelings or meaning , gives a partial or uncertain answer - knows something felt off , but maybe not exactly why . Self - explanations are incomplete : ’ I don ’ t really know , it just bothered me .’ Does not volunteer analysis unprompted . - High : Is capable of self - analysis and meaning making . Can describe how something felt at the time and how they understand it now , and can identify internal contradictions . Note : this analysis applies to experiences already established in the conversation - reflexivity does not introduce new facts or events . Disclosure - Low : Keeps personal feelings and private life to themselves - even when directly asked . For emotional or introspective questions , the deflecting phrase IS the complete answer - not a phrase appended after already sharing the feeling . ’ I just deal with it ’ means that is all that is said , not that more follows . For questions about personal wellbeing - health , energy , home life , relationships : one brief closed sentence , then done . For questions probing what they haven ’ t shared or how things really feel : stays vague and closed , does not open up . Treats the interviewer as a stranger who hasn ’ t earned the private story . - Medium : Shares factual and neutral things readily but is cautious about anything personal or sensitive , especially early on . Gives measured answers on tender subjects with someone just met . May warm up slightly as the conversation goes on . - High : Does not have an issue sharing personal content , and will present it plainly when relevant . When asked what they haven ’ t said out loud , actually says it . Does not soften before diving into difficult content . Understanding - Low : Answers what questions literally ask , not what they ’ re really getting at . When a question has both a surface reading and a deeper intended meaning , takes the surface one - answers at the practical or descriptive level rather than the personal or meaning - making one . A question about how something changed the person gets answered with what changed in their circumstances or behavior , not how they changed inside . A question about whether they feel something gets answered with whether that thing practically applies to them , not whether they feel it . The mismatch is subtle and earnest - just consistently off - register . Does not stop to ask what was really meant . - Medium : Usually follows questions but occasionally interprets them narrower or broader than intended . If something is genuinely ambiguous , asks once rather than guessing . - High : Correctly interprets the intent behind questions and clarifies ambiguities in questions .

blocks.en: B.3 Expert Ratings of Realism and Trait Presence
blocks.zh: B.3 现实主义和存在障碍的专家评分

blocks.en: To assess InterviewPlayground’s ability to believably simulate participants with different levels of knowledge, understanding, memory, verbosity, reflexivity, and disclosure, we collect expert judgments from three annotators with experience in qualitative research in three different domains: sociology, public health, and human-computer interaction. We begin by taking a random stratified sample of 50 human interviews and 50 simulated interviews from § 5 . We use a stratified sample to ensure a balanced representation of participant traits in the simulated interviews and a balanced representation of interview topics in both the human and simulated interviews. Then, we take a random six-turn excerpt from each interview and have annotators rate the participant’s knowledge, understanding, memory, verbosity, disclosure, and reflexivity as either low, medium, or high. They also rate the realism of each participant on a 4-point scale from “Not realistic” to “Highly realistic.” Annotators were informed that there was a mix of real and fake transcripts, but the transcripts were not labeled and were presented in a random order.
blocks.zh: 为了评估InterviewPlayground以不同水平的知识、理解、记忆、动词、反射和披露对参与者进行可信模拟的能力,我们收集了三个在社会学、公共卫生和人与计算机互动三个不同领域具有定性研究经验的注释家的专家判断。 我们从第5节开始随机抽取50个人类访谈和50个模拟访谈的分层样本。 我们使用分层抽样,以确保模拟访谈中参与者特征的均衡表现,以及在人和模拟访谈中对访谈主题的均衡表现。 然后,我们从每次采访中随机抽取一个6个回合的节选,并让注释者将参与者的知识、理解、记忆、动词、披露和反射性评为低、中或高。 他们还将每个参与者的现实主义从“不现实”到“高度现实”的四分级评定。 注释员被告知,有真假笔录的混合,但笔录没有被贴上标签并按随机顺序呈现.

blocks.en: To determine whether expert annotators can correctly identify the behavioral traits that the simulated participants are intended to exhibit, we compare the expert ratings to the assigned value of the trait for the 50 simulated interview excerpts. We use Krippendorff’s alpha to calculate the agreement among the annotators and the agreement between the median annotator rating and the assigned value of the simulation. We find that expert annotators can identify knowledge, understanding, reflexivity, verbosity, and disclosure ( Table 3 ). However, they struggle to identify the memory level of the participant, which is unsurprising as annotators did not have access to the memory bank. We additionally find that expert annotators rate simulated participants as realistic as human participants, with an average rating of 3.51 3.51 compared to 3.34 3.34 for human participants, a difference that is insignificant ( p = 0.28 p=0.28 , t = 1.08 t=1.08 ).

blocks.en: B.4 Estimating Interview Time
blocks.zh: B.4 估计面谈时间

blocks.en: To estimate the elapsed time of an interview in InterviewPlayground, we add the wall-clock time required for the interviewer to generate a question to an estimate of how long it would take a participant to respond. To calculate this estimate, we estimate the number of syllables in the response using Textstat. 3 3 3 https://textstat.org/ We then multiply the number of syllables by a speaking rate and add a constant to account for delays before participants speak. To calculate these speaking rates and constants, we use an empirical estimate from the 16,676 responses that we recorded from 450 interview participants in § 5.1 . However, because more verbose participants tend to speak faster ( Yuan et al., 2006 ) , we also adjust the speaking rates based on participant verbosity. Specifically, we first use k-means clustering over all 16,676 response to group responses into 3 different length categories. We then use a Theil-Sen regression to estimate the speaking rate and constant for each of these three groups. This process produces speaking rates of 167.7 167.7 , 189.5 189.5 , and 216.1 216.1 syllables per minute and delays of 11.3 11.3 , 16 16 , and 26.6 26.6 seconds for the low, medium, and high verbosity responses respectively. When we calculate the elapsed time of an interview in InterviewPlayground, we set the speaking rate and delay according to the verbosity level of the simulated participant.
blocks.zh: 为了估计在InterviewPlayground接受采访的时间,我们把采访者提出问题所需的时长加为估计参与者需要多长时间才能作出答复。 为了计算这一估计数,我们使用Textstat估算答复中的音节数。 3 3 3 https://textstat.org/ 然后,我们将音节数乘以发言率,并增加一个常数,以说明与会者发言之前的延误情况。 在计算这些演讲率和常数时,我们使用我们从第5.1节450位访谈参与者中记录的16 676个答复中得出的实证估计。 然而,由于更多的动词参与者往往说话速度快(Yuan等,2006年),我们也根据参与者的动词来调整演讲率. 具体地说,我们首先使用k-指将所有16,676个响应对分组响应分组为3个不同的长度类别. 然后我们用Theil-Sen回归法来估计这三个组中的每个组的演讲率和常数. 这一过程产生了每分钟167.7个167.7个、189.5个189.5个和216.1个216.1个音节的发声率,低、中、高马鞭草反应的发声率分别为11.3个11.3个、16个16个和26.6个26.6秒。 当我们在"InterviewPlayground"(InterviewPlayground)中计算一次采访的经过时间时,我们根据模拟参与者的动词水平来设定演讲率和延迟.

blocks.en: B.5 Estimating Trait Proportions
blocks.zh: B.5 估计轨迹比例

blocks.en: To construct each of InterviewPlayground’s three simulation settings, we create a sample of 30 simulated participants intended to represent the target population of the study. To set the behavioral traits for this sample, we first estimate their proportions based on survey self-reports of participant traits for all human studies with the same target population in § 5.1 . Rather than use self-reports for verbosity, we use k-means clustering to group all 450 participants into three groups based on the average number of words in their responses. Then, we calculate the proportions of participants based on how these three groups are represented within each target population. After calculating these estimates, we use constrained random assignment to set the trait values of our 30 simulated participants to be proportional to the estimated trait values of the 150 participants in the same target population. Rather than considering interactions between traits, we treat them as independent.
blocks.zh: 为了构建InterviewPlayground的三个模拟设置,我们创建了30个模拟参与者的样本,旨在代表研究的目标人群. 为了确定这一样本的行为特征,我们首先根据对第5.1节中具有相同目标人群的所有人类研究参与者特征的调查自报来估计其比例。 我们不是用自报来形容动词,而是用克-指将所有450名参与者按他们答复中的平均单词数分组为三组. 然后,我们根据这三个群体在每一目标群体中的代表性情况计算出参与者的比例。 在计算这些估计数后,我们使用有限的随机分配来确定我们30个模拟参与者的特征值与同一目标人群150个参与者的估计特征值成正比。 我们不考虑特征之间的相互作用,而是把他们视为独立的。

blocks.en: C.2 Human Validation
blocks.zh: C.2 人类验证

blocks.en: To validate the LLM judges for InterviewReportCard, we collect 1,800 expert judgments from three annotators with experience in qualitative research. Each annotator rates 50 excerpts from interviews with human participants and 50 excerpts from interviews with simulated participants from the experiments in § 5.1 . We then apply Gemini 3.1 Pro to the same excerpts, using the same information and scoring rubrics provided to the human annotators. For coherence, adaptiveness, leading questions, support and rapport, and unclear questions, we calculate Krippendorff’s alpha to measure agreement among human annotators and agreement between the median human rating and the LLM judge rating. We find moderate agreement among human annotators and comparable agreement between the median human rating and the LLM judge rating ( Table 4 ).
blocks.zh: 为了验证LLM法官的采访报告卡,我们收集了3名具有定性研究经验的专家判决书。 每个注释者对50个与人类参与者面谈的节选和50个与模拟参与者面谈的节选进行第5.1节中的实验。 然后我们把双子座3.1 Pro应用到同样的节选上,使用提供给人类注释者的相同信息和评分分分号. 关于一致性、适应性、领先问题、支持和关系以及不明确的问题,我们计算出Krippendorff的α,以衡量人类注释者之间的一致,以及人类中位值和LLM评分之间的一致。 我们发现,人类注释者之间有适度的一致意见,而人评分中位数与LLM法官评分中位数之间有相当的一致(表4)。
